leads.summary: Open PR #13166's chamfer mask clips this PR's BorderSurface shadows if their implementations are combined unchanged
leads.location: shell/Ui/BorderSurface.qml:33-40; open PR #13166 patch to shell/Ui/BorderSurface.qml (pr-13166-selected.txt:220-245)
leads.consequence: For a theme with triangular corners (Style.cornerChamfer and radius > 0) and enabled surface shadows, #13166 renders the whole BorderSurface into a default item-sized layer, then masks that layer to the chamfered card. The negative-z shadow Loader from #13191 is inside that same BorderSurface. Its outside-card pixels cannot survive the layer's default sourceRect and mask. Thus enabled outer shadows disappear on chamfered cards after both changes are integrated, while the shadow geometry/window padding may still be reserved. Their edits also overlap in BorderSurface, requiring explicit reconciliation. Put the shadow in an unmasked sibling layer and adapt its shape when integrating, or explicitly design a shared expanded sourceRect and mask.

leads.summary: Live shadow-margin changes leave an already-open MultiSelect at its old maximum height
leads.consequence: For a long list opened near the bottom with shadows initially off, changing [popups] shadow-alpha to enable the default shadow changes bottomMargin to 31 while _availableBelow retains its old 12-pixel clearance, because reposition() is called only on opening and trigger geometry changes. Qt repositions on the margin change without recomputing _availableBelow and can slide the too-tall popup upwards, overlapping the trigger by up to about 19 logical pixels. Reopening recalculates it. This is an exported primitive (qmldir:16), but no shipped MultiSelect call site was found; relevant to external plugin consumers. Recompute on bottomMarginChanged and on containing window height changes.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (edge notes); corroborated; kept private (live toggle while open, no in-tree users)

leads.summary: Valid TOML exponent notation for shadow numbers is silently omitted by the shared parser
leads.consequence: A valid TOML override such as [popups] shadow-alpha = 1e-1 is neither a quoted string, plain decimal, width list, nor bare word in parseShell; it is dropped. ShadowGeometry.spec then receives missing alpha and disables the shadow, rather than applying 0.1. A finite shadow-blur = 1e2 similarly falls back to 24 instead of using 100. This diverges from the new documentation's finite-number clamping rule and fails silently; extend the shared parser for valid TOML numeric notation (and keep the geometry parser's coercion aligned), or document the accepted lexical subset and test it.
leads.triage: dropped: shared Color.qml parser unchanged by this PR; pre-existing, outside scope

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier automated review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13191#issuecomment-5838760932) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13191#issuecomment-5850243765), checked at `b67e9333`.

**Verified:** all six earlier points are addressed at `b67e9333`, and the follow-up commit introduced no new material issue. One interaction with another open PR is noted below.

| Earlier point | Outcome at `b67e9333` |
| --- | --- |
| Popups near a screen edge move inward | Resolved: now documented in `docs/theming.md` and the `PopupCard` comment |
| `MultiSelect` popup pushed over its trigger | Resolved (executed, see below) |
| Stacked toast shadows | Resolved: `docs/theming.md` now notes the overlap with translucent backgrounds |
| `BorderSurface` cost with no shadow section | Resolved (executed, see below) |
| Render test aborts without a GL context | Resolved: the new probe exits non-zero and the test skips (source-confirmed, not executed) |
| Render test sample outside the padded area | Resolved: `y=229` is inside the reserved area, so the check can now fail |

**Verified, `MultiSelect`:** isolated Qt 6.11.2 QML engine run, 400 px window, long list, trigger bottom at y=278, default `[popups]` shadow geometry:

```text
revision   shadows   popup y range   result
418e6e0c   on        261 to 369      moved up 19 px, covers the trigger
b67e9333   on        280 to 369      below the trigger, ends at the 31 px margin
all three  off       280 to 388      identical at merge-base, 418e6e0c and b67e9333
```

With shadows off, Qt's default `bottomMargin` is -1, so the new `Math.max(Style.space(12), bottomMargin)` reduces to the old value.

**Verified, `BorderSurface`:** surfaces without a `shadowSection` no longer resolve a shadow spec. For 4000 such surfaces, creation took 49 ms at `b67e9333` versus 44 ms before the PR and 108 ms at `418e6e0c`. A shell.toml change no longer re-evaluates them (81 ms at `418e6e0c`). No in-tree code reads `BorderSurface.shadowSpec` outside `BorderSurface`, and switching `shadowSection` between a section and `""` at runtime produced no QML warnings. The new source assertions in `surface-shadow-test.sh` fail when either the `BorderSurface` or the `MultiSelect` change is reverted.

**Docs wording:** a card already held a few pixels from the edge by `PopupCard`'s own margin moves only by the part of its pad that crosses the edge, not the full shadow extent, so "by up to the shadow extent" would be exact.

**Correction to the earlier review:** it said toast shadow overlap is "only visible with translucent `[notifications]` backgrounds". Each lower toast is drawn after the one above, so its shadow also falls faintly over the bottom edge of an opaque toast above it (about 2 to 4 % tint at the bottom row with the documented example and acceptance-test settings, computed from Qt's shadow constants). That is negligible; the translucent case remains the visible one and the new docs note covers it.

### Combined with open PR #13166, shadows drawn inside chamfered `BorderSurface`s disappear

Open PR #13166 ("Mirror Hyprland triangular corners in shell surfaces") also edits `shell/Ui/BorderSurface.qml`. The two PRs merge without a textual conflict, and the merged file keeps both additions:

```text
BorderSurface (root Rectangle)
├─ layer.enabled: chamfered              #13166: item-sized layer + MultiEffect chamfer mask
├─ chamferMask
├─ Loader { z: -1; SurfaceShadow }       #13191: shadow drawn outside the card bounds
└─ border overlay Loader
```

In Qt 6.9 and 6.11 an enabled layer hides the item's subtree and draws it only through a texture of the item's own `0,0,width,height` rectangle when `layer.sourceRect` is unset. The chamfer mask then keeps only the cut outline. The outer shadow lies outside that rectangle, so on a chamfered surface it is not drawn. This follows from Qt source and a textual merge of the two heads; it was not rendered.

**Impact:** only when both PRs land as written and Hyprland uses triangular corners (non-zero `rounding` with `rounding_power` at most 1.0; the in-tree defaults do not). Every shadow-opted `BorderSurface` with a non-zero radius (all in-tree ones except button tooltips) then shows no shadow, including `PopupCard` and the bar tooltip, while their windows still reserve the transparent pad and still slide inward at a screen edge. Small corner slivers between the 45° cut and the shadow's rounded interior mask can also tint translucent fills (computed, not rendered). The lock field and notification toasts draw their shadow as a sibling outside the surface and keep it. Neither PR's current tests detect the combination.

**Suggested change:** for whichever PR lands second, draw the shadow outside the masked subtree (for example as a sibling, as the lock screen and notifications already do, or by moving the chamfer layer onto an inner fill item) and give `SurfaceShadow`'s interior mask the chamfered outline when chamfered. Enlarging `layer.sourceRect` alone would not help, because the chamfer mask is sized to the item.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the follow-up commit, all consumers of `BorderSurface.shadowSpec` and `MultiSelect`, the changed tests, and the relevant Qt 6.9.3/6.11.2, qtbase 6.11.2 offscreen plugin and Quickshell v0.3.1 source. In an isolated sandbox: `surface-shadow-test.sh` at `b67e9333` and against single-change reverts, and Qt 6.11.2 QML engine checks (software backend, offscreen) of the production `shell/Commons` and `shell/Ui` files (with stub Quickshell modules) for `MultiSelect` geometry, the `null` shadow path and a creation benchmark. For #13166, a textual merge of both heads and the two PRs' shadow and border-geometry tests on the merged tree (both pass). No pixels were captured or inspected, no GL renderer ran, and no live or nested desktop session was used. The PySide6 render test stopped at its PySide6 check, and the edge slide was not re-run; the edge behavior relies on source and the author's measurement. Tint figures are computed from Qt source constants.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
